fr.elements: Main Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Driveway; Internal Drive Aisle; Landscaped Area; Front Entry Area; Pedestrian Walkways; Street Frontage; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation; Vehicle Congestion
fr.recommendations: Based on the observed site conditions, maintaining clear and unobstructed pathways through available access points could improve overall responder movement throughout the property. Vehicle congestion within parking areas may affect apparatus positioning and staging, so preserving adequate maneuvering lanes along the internal drive aisle would support efficient emergency operations. Dense vegetation near the landscaped areas and open green space could reduce visibility for approaching personnel, and periodic management of that vegetation may enhance responder sightlines. Limited access to the rear of the main building would benefit from pre-incident familiarity, as identifying the most effective approach route in advance may assist personnel during time-sensitive response activities at that portion of the structure.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Limited Defensible Space; Vegetation Adjacent to Access Route; Irrigated Landscape; Open Fuel Break
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing direct vegetation contact with the structure by creating and maintaining separation between combustible shrubs, brush, and tree clusters and the building perimeter could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity in the immediate structure zone. Managing scattered trees and mixed vegetation cover to increase spacing between individual plants and canopy layers may reduce opportunities for fire to move through connected fuels toward improvements. Removing or thinning brush and shrubs that are directly adjacent to the structure would further support defensible space within the near-structure perimeter. Maintaining and expanding the existing open fuel break could support suppression operations and reduce fuel continuity across the property. Continued management of vegetation growing along the access route would support firefighter access and improve navigation during emergency response. Preserving and expanding the irrigated landscape near the structure may reduce fuel availability in the immediate perimeter and contribute to long-term wildfire resilience.
